limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.

Only the existing llama.cpp NUMA/thread slice is normalized at 3e390af18de1131dda27913c00511725b4274c8a; other original sources remain unnormalized, with their identities and limits retained in the procedure/readsets.
Linux NUMA source paths and separate configuration controls do not establish universally optimal thread counts, affinity combinations or measured placement gains.

applicability.scope: Prepare and record CPU/NUMA process placement, phase-specific thread settings, device contention and environment prerequisites before shared-host performance measurements.
applicability.prerequisites: No outstanding hard environment errors: required devices/driver, planned device count and any container prerequisites must be present before running.
applicability.input_contract: Current affinity/NUMA policy, accelerator locality, workload phase/thread controls, device occupancy, runtime environment and relevant container/resource limits.
applicability.produced_artifact: A recorded placement/thread/environment configuration and preflight outcome, with errors requiring remediation and warnings retained for the measurement campaign.
applicability.failure_modes: Changing affinity or thread settings between rounds confounds timing; combining independent affinity mechanisms is order-sensitive, and small driver memory usage can be mistaken for device occupation.

recommendations: Inspect affinity and NUMA policy before placement and hold them constant across comparisons; document and requalify a round when placement changes.
Choose one affinity-mask authority and distinguish generation, batch and frontend thread controls; source template thread counts are starting points rather than tuned constants.
Record device occupancy and structured ERROR/WARNING results before measuring, using the official environment setup for derived CANN paths.
